target_customer: Gig workers, freelancers, digital workers and small businesses in Mexico who must file monthly taxes
problem: Millions of independent workers in Mexico face monthly SAT filing duties without tax knowledge, and accountants charge far more than they can easily pay.
business_model: Consumer and SME subscription for tax filing, e-invoicing (CFDI) and tax document management with accountant support; early bundle also included insurance

founders.name: Stiven Rodriguez Sanchez
previous_startups: Qualtri (OYO-style hospitality idea, dropped after pivot)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he joined Uber in 2014 and helped grow Latin America from 3 cities to over 150; TechCrunch and LAVCA say he is from Colombia.

founders.name: Mateo Jaramillo
previous_startups: Qualtri (OYO-style hospitality idea, dropped after pivot)
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch (December 2020) and the LAVCA interview; not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires integration with Mexico's SAT tax and invoicing systems, rules for monthly filings and later AI features; standard engineering with regulatory complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Tax filing history and invoices create some lock-in, but accountants and other software could offer the same service.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Accountants charging about 25 to 30 dollars were the alternative cited in December 2020; Mercado Pago later publishes freelancer tax guidance and invoicing features, but no incumbent bought Heru in the sources found.

market_need_then: Mexico requires monthly tax filing from independent workers; in December 2020 TechCrunch cited about 20,000 people waiting during a soft launch with 1,200 accepted users, and the company priced tax service at about 5 dollars a month versus accountants at 25 to 30.

branding.name_origin: From the Yanomami people of the Venezuela-Brazil border, where Heru means something or someone who protects (LAVCA interview with the founders)

identity.voice_and_tone: Protective, simple framing for gig workers: easy, transparent and automated (YC description)

branding.brand_signature: Heru Casas: physical rest spaces in Mexico City where gig workers charge phones and use bathrooms with the app
branding.community_and_virality: Heru Casas helped find early users per TechCrunch; no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: A meaningful, short name with a physical community touchpoint (Heru Casas) that drew early users, plus coverage in TechCrunch and Mexican business press; no evidence of broad brand-driven growth.

pivots.from: Qualtri, a hospitality idea modeled on OYO Rooms
pivots.to: Heru, software services for Latin American gig workers (insurance, credit, tax)
pivots.why: OYO already operated in Mexico with a large team; founders spent three months brainstorming and scored 371 ideas (LAVCA, TechCrunch)

pivots.from: Gig worker bundle with Heru Casas hubs, insurance and credit
pivots.to: Tax filing and e-invoicing platform for independent workers and SMEs
pivots.why: Not stated; LAVCA notes the product expanded from Heru Casa hubs to tax filing software and insurance

outcome_analysis: Heru began as Qualtri, an OYO-style idea, dropped it after finding OYO in Mexico, and pivoted to services for gig workers, then focused on tax automation. It raised 1.7 million pre-seed in 2020 and a 6 million seed led by Gradient Ventures in September 2022, and is active with about 53 people. Sources do not show later rounds or revenue, so scale is unverified.
notes: Competitor list left empty: no source dated near the batch was found. TechCrunch (December 2020) says OYO was the incumbent for the original idea and accountants charging 25 to 30 dollars were the alternative; those sources are over a year after the batch. The 1.7M pre-seed was raised in two parts, 500K in February 2020 and 1.2M shortly before December 2020. The 6M seed is stated by Axios, PR Newswire, LatamList and others. Founded year conflicts: YC page says 2020, one search summary says 2019; the S19 batch implies the original company existed in 2019. Education not found. Sources disagree on Stiven's surname (Rodriguez or Sanchez). Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs; an Ecosistema Startup headline says Heru is burning cash again to grow, date not verified.
